clue.text: Notice if floor is damp

parts.note: surface reading: an observation that the floor happens to be wet
setter's reading: a printed warning sign, the kind propped up on a freshly mopped floor

explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a verb telling you to spot something; it is a noun, the yellow warning sign put out on wet floors.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the exact wording of the standard caution sign placed where a mopped surface could make people fall.

clue.text: It prevents disclosure of a comedian's routine, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a court injunction forbidding publication
second meaning: the sequence in which a comic tells the jokes

explanation.surface: A legal ban stops anyone revealing a comic's act.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second half as the order of the gags in a set; 'perhaps' flags that this is a playful sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal injunction banning publication of information is called this, and it also literally describes how jokes are sequenced.

clue.text: In self-conscious surroundings a king is unreliable

indicators.note: surroundings enclose something, so the self-conscious word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: shy people are self-conscious
taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An awkward, bashful monarch can't be depended on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shaky is wobbly and insecure, so it cannot be trusted or relied upon; a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: They may display welcome for those suffering ill-treatment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: mats at the front door, often printed with the word welcome
second meaning: people who let others walk all over them

explanation.surface: Abused people are made to look welcoming.
explanation.definitionFit: Front-door mats often say welcome, and figuratively the word means submissive people others trample on.

clue.text: Parts of Bristol remain backward for wine

indicators.note: going backward means those letters are read from right to left
only parts of the following words are used, so the answer lies across them

parts.note: the end of the city name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: Bits of a West Country city stay behind in the past, to suit a drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: BrisTOL REMain holds TOLREM, which reads MERLOT from the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: Merlot is a red grape variety and the red drink made from it, an example of the category.

clue.text: Film equipment captures dangerous liquid turning into vapour

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: steam is water vapour

indicators.note: something turning changes position, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: acid is a corrosive, hazardous liquid

explanation.surface: A camera rig films a hazardous chemical evaporating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captures' and 'into' both point the same way: the shuffled liquid ends up within the vapour.
explanation.definitionFit: A Steadicam is a stabilising body mount that lets an operator carry a movie camera smoothly while walking.

clue.text: Stir up negative response to teacher under pressure

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under means following below, so these pieces come after

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means these letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the word that refuses
what pupils call a male schoolteacher

explanation.surface: A pupil causes trouble by answering back to a pressured teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir up' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'Stir' alone is the definition and 'up' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is old British slang for jail, as in doing time in stir, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Distribute funny tweets over a continuous period

definitions.note: the answer is usually an adverb or adjective, round the clock

indicators.note: to distribute is to spread out and deal around, so the letters are dealt into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Someone posts amusing social media messages nonstop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'Distribute' does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means all day every day, every hour of the week without a break.

clue.text: To Holmes, a criminal is repugnant

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent, so these letters are bent out of order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes finds a lawbreaker disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something so vile that it provokes disgust and strong aversion; direct synonyms.

clue.text: Confuse shy host

definitions.meaning: second meaning: hurl, as at a coconut shy
third meaning: put on, as when you hold a party

explanation.surface: Bewilder a bashful entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings: 'shy' is the verb meaning to fling, not the adjective bashful.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers disconcerting someone, flinging an object, and staging a party, as in throwing a bash.

clue.text: Fool puts cheap wine before the Queen

indicators.note: coming before means placed in front, so the first piece leads

parts.note: plonk is British slang for cheap wine
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: An idiot serves bargain-bin wine to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A plonker is British slang for an idiot, popularised by the sitcom Only Fools and Horses.

clue.text: Praised heart in warrior making contact

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a lion is a brave fighter, as in a lionheart

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so only the middle letters of that word are kept

parts.note: the three central letters of the word

explanation.surface: A soldier with a celebrated heart reaches out to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of LION opens to take the AIS from the heart of Praised.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a working link or channel of communication between people or groups, so it means contact.

clue.text: Quickly turn around every document demanding your initials

indicators.note: initials are opening letters, so each word gives only its first

parts.note: the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Rush through every form that asks you to sign with your initials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'your initials' looks like the thing being demanded, but 'initials' is the instruction and 'your' is one of the four words.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to eddy is to whirl or swirl rapidly in a circle, like water in a current.

clue.text: Studio boss who could animate any wild set

indicators.note: to animate is to set in motion, so these letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A film mogul could bring even the craziest scenery to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' looks like the anagram signal but its letters are needed; 'animate', apt for a cartoon maker, does the job.
explanation.definitionFit: The founder of the famous animation company headed the studio behind Mickey Mouse and early cartoon features.

clue.text: Start eating, it's fantastic!

indicators.note: something fantastic is fanciful and unreal, so these letters are made into something new

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A diner tucks in and declares the food wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start eating' reads as an invitation to tuck in; 'Start' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate is to initiate or set something going, such as an inquiry or a fight.

clue.text: Hear wife has little ones making containers for tackle

indicators.note: hearing means taking the words by their sound rather than their spelling

parts.note: a spouse plus runts, the small members of a litter; has just joins them

explanation.surface: A man learns his spouse has had babies, which makes for a family fishing kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Tackle is British slang for a man's genitals; Y-fronts are classic British men's briefs.
explanation.definitionFit: These close-fitting men's briefs, with an inverted Y seam, hold a man's private parts, jokingly called his tackle.

clue.text: Identify smell as something with no real effect

parts.note: to place someone is to recognise them
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: Pinning down an odour turns out to be pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy pill with no active ingredient, given in trials to compare against real medication.

clue.text: Introduction for record by rising European group

indicators.note: by means beside, so the pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: pro is Latin for in favour of
a log is a written record

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means these letters are read upwards

parts.note: the European Union

explanation.surface: An opening track for an album by an up-and-coming band from the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: A prologue is the opening section of a play, book or poem that leads into the main work.

clue.text: Old flame still sounds happy

indicators.note: sounds means the words are said out loud and spelt differently

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
static means motionless

explanation.surface: A former partner who stays put seems cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic means overjoyed, a stronger degree of happiness rather than an exact synonym.

clue.text: Without this star, we should all be dead

parts.words: Without this star, we should all be dead
parts.note: surface reading: a celestial body, like the sun, that keeps life going
setter's reading: the beat of the organ in your chest, without which nobody lives; star is the idol meaning

explanation.walkthrough: 'star' suggests the sun; it is a celebrity idol, and the life-or-death part is the pulse in the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart-throb is a handsome celebrity who sets fans' pulses racing, so a star in the showbiz sense.

clue.text: Comic character shaped like Bowie?

parts.note: the shape of a bow is an arch
the singer's name once its first three letters are swapped out

explanation.surface: A cartoon figure modelled on the singer David Bowie.
explanation.walkthrough: Read Bowie as BOW plus IE: replace the bow with its shape, an arch.
explanation.definitionFit: Archie Andrews is the red-haired teenage hero of the long-running American comic-book series.

clue.text: Present state excludes a non-orthodox view

parts.note: present, as in attending

indicators.note: to exclude is to leave out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to state is to say
taken as written; this is the letter left out

explanation.surface: The current government bans unorthodox opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present state' reads as the current situation, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is a belief contrary to accepted church doctrine, an opinion departing from established teaching.

clue.text: Addict getting friendly description of simple instructions

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who takes drugs
second meaning: the word that goes before friendly when instructions are easy to follow

explanation.surface: A drug taker is handed an easy guide.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a fill-in-the-blank: put the answer before friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is slang for a drug taker, and user-friendly describes manuals or software that are easy to operate.

clue.text: Decline to provide cover, if perimeter is lost

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so the inner letters of the edge word disappear
to provide a cover is to fit it in place, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: SIDE, an edge making up a perimeter, with its middle gone
a lid covers a container

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to stand in for a colleague if the boundary goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is loose: LID sits inside S_E, the outside of SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A slide is a fall or downturn, as in prices sliding, so it means a decline.

clue.text: Negative outcome of narrow failure with organic treatment

parts.note: the negative reply
a roll of tobacco leaf, a plant product given a treatment

explanation.surface: Organic medicine narrowly fails and produces a bad result.
explanation.walkthrough: From 'close, but no cigar', said of a near miss.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom close but no cigar is said when an attempt nearly succeeds but still falls short.

clue.text: Out of office working with permission

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
leave is permission, as in by your leave

explanation.surface: Someone working away from the office has been allowed to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' seems to contradict 'Out of office'; it gives the small word ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on leave is on authorised absence from their job, so they are away from the workplace.

clue.text: Order forecast without any publicity

indicators.note: without means lacking, so some letters are taken away

parts.note: to forecast is to predict
PR is public relations; these letters go

explanation.surface: Someone foretells events while avoiding the press.
explanation.walkthrough: PR stands for public relations, the publicity business.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree or proclamation issued by an authority, so it is a command.

clue.text: Healthy edge a politician needs to get coverage

definitions.text: a politician needs to get coverage

parts.note: sound means in good health
a sharp edge or bite in someone's tone

explanation.surface: A politician must look fit and sharp to win media attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A short catchy quote that broadcasters clip is what a politician must supply for airtime on the news.
